analysis.title: Global Markets Weekly Wrap-Up, October 31, 2026
key_insights: Steno Research data shows the largest de-grossing of equity long/short funds since its data began in 2016. Friday Oct 30 had the feel of forced liquidation across assets.
For the week, the Russell 2000 gained 1.30%, the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.00%, the Dow fell 0.85% and the S&P 500 fell 0.57%. Large-cap value beat growth for a fourth straight week.
AI stocks rallied early in the week, then reversed after Alphabet and Amazon results renewed concerns about the returns on large-scale capex.

In October the Nasdaq 100 fell about 3.3% and is on course for its largest monthly underperformance against the equal-weight S&P since 2001. Mag7 fell over 6% on the month while the S&P ex-AI rose 0.7%.
The Broad AI basket fell over 13% in October, its largest drop ever, while SPX ex-AI gained 7.5%. NeoClouds fell 37% on the month.
Goldman's basket of companies seen as most at risk from AI gained over 15%, erasing more than half of the AI beneficiaries' gains since the launch of ChatGPT.
UBS traders describe the move as capital rotating out of crowded AI and growth into value, small caps, consumer and rate-sensitive cyclicals rather than leaving equities.
Alphabet revenue rose 25% to $127.6B and Cloud more than doubled, but EPS was $2.12 against roughly $3 expected. An $8.7B paper loss on AI investments drove more than half of the miss.

Alphabet Cloud revenue was $30.7B vs $29.1B expected (+103% y/y). Search, YouTube, Subscriptions and Services missed. Search grew 12% vs a ~14% buyside bogey and Search fell below 50% of revenue for the first time.
Alphabet's CFO said it began using third-party compute at the end of Q3 and will ramp it in Q4. It expects near-term margin headwinds and significantly higher 2027 capex.
Amazon fell about 10% after hours on an EPS and revenue miss, while AWS accelerated and posted $17.77B of Q3 operating income, up 55%.

The four largest hyperscalers reported combined quarterly capex above $200B (AMZN ~$77B, GOOGL ~$51B, MSFT ~$39B, META ~$34B). Hyperscaler CDS hit record wides and Goldman credit strategists say AI default risk has tripled since January.
Intel fell over 20% after its CFO said 2027 will not be a year of positive free cash flow. ServiceNow fell 24% on a Q3 profit miss, its worst day ever.
Elon Musk warned that debt markets have shut off funding for companies without substantial non-AI-datacenter revenue, and that the 200+ neoclouds face heavy failures and consolidation.
CalPERS reportedly cut its Mag 7 exposure by 26% and is shifting toward private equity.
SK Hynix Q3 revenue rose 328% y/y to ₩104.62T vs ₩98.23T expected. Operating profit rose 632% y/y to ₩83.33T. The company says it is sold out of DRAM and HBM through 2029.
Semiconductors are trading at record-low forward P/E levels. Alphabet is at its lowest P/E ever.

The 10Y Treasury touched 5.36% on Oct 7, the highest since 2002, and traded down to 4.88% on Oct 30, about 35-40bp lower on the month. Bonds beat stocks by about 2 percentage points in October per Goldman.

Fed December hike pricing slipped to about 70% from 95% mid-month. The Fed, ECB and BoJ held rates. Fed Chair Warsh said rates are having an effect on the technology complex and noted wider credit spreads.

The BoJ held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote and said underlying inflation is consistent with 2% for the first time since 2013. It raised its FY2027 inflation forecast to 2.6%. The ECB held at 2.50% with a possible final hike in December, and Lagarde reportedly plans to leave early.

Brazil sold off sharply after Lula's election win: the stock market fell 17.6% in one day, the real fell 11% and the 10Y yield rose from 12.9% to 16%. A voting extension ordered by a judge raises legal questions about the result.
Gold fell over 6% in October and broke below $4,000 on forced liquidation. GLD had its largest weekly outflow since March. Silver fell 18.5% to below $50.
Bitcoin fell to near $76,000 from above $86,000 on Oct 5. Binance was reportedly hacked for up to $6.3B, with about $3B frozen, and Binance says it will cover all losses.

The Iran war is in its eighth month with a US naval blockade and Houthi attacks on Saudi targets. Reports suggest US-Israeli strikes after the Nov 3 midterms. Saudi crude exports are back above 7M bpd.
Deutsche Bank notes Oct 27 has historically marked the final seasonal low for the S&P 500, which rose over the following three months in 21 of the past 23 midterm years.
Anthropic's S-1 reportedly shows $2.08 of revenue per $1 of compute spend, up from $0.40 in Q1 2025, and the company is described as profitable.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 EPS of $2.12 missed the roughly $3 expected, and Search and YouTube missed. Cloud beat at $30.7B vs $29.1B expected. Capex rises significantly in 2027.
Fell about 10% after hours on an earnings double miss despite AWS acceleration, with AWS operating income up 55% to $17.77B.
Fell over 20% on earnings after the CFO said 2027 free cash flow will not be positive and the PC slowdown continues through 1H 2027.
Fell 24% after a Q3 profit miss, its worst day ever.
Reportedly offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees while keeping headcount near 223,000.
Fell more than 26% intraday as Brazil sold off after Lula's election win.
Rose 16% in five hours on reports that the NYSE owner plans a regulated US market for 24/7 perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid.
Recorded its largest weekly outflow since March after gold fell below $4,000.

sector_views.rationale: AI and growth names are being de-grossed on funding and capex return concerns, though semis trade at record-low forward P/E.
UBS traders describe a rotation into value, small caps, consumer and rate-sensitive cyclicals.
Mercedes joined BMW and VW in cutting its outlook, with a car margin target of 2-3% vs up to 5% before, on China weakness.

Amazon Q3: reported an earnings double miss and the stock fell about 10% after hours. AWS operating income was $17.77B, up 55%.
SK Hynix Q3 reported: revenue ₩104.62T vs ₩98.23T expected, operating profit ₩83.33T, net profit ₩39.78T (+216% y/y).

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is strong: Cloud revenue more than doubled at Alphabet, AWS accelerated, SK Hynix is sold out of DRAM and HBM through 2029, and Anthropic reportedly earns $2.08 per $1 of compute spend. Semis trade at record-low forward P/E.
